q: Two exposed GitHub tokens are still not rotated, and there is no rotation policy for the eleven secrets.
r: Rotate the two exposed tokens yourself (Claude must not touch token values). Adopt the proposed policy: rotate on a leak, when someone leaves, and yearly.

q: An old frontmatter project is still on your personal Vercel team, 48 days since its last deploy.
r: Re-link everything to the company team, then retire the old project. Deleting it is permanent, so it waits for your yes.

q: Is there an intellectual property agreement between the founders?
r: Nobody can check this but you and Amit. Sign one before the first stranger's document is stored.

q: When a person accepts a change, the file is stamped "verified by". What name goes in the stamp?
r: Their public handle, written human:<handle>. Not their email, which every published page would expose, and not an internal id nobody can read.

q: On Free, does syncing to GitHub use up the 20 pushes a month?
r: Yes. Free never pushes to GitHub automatically; each push is a button the person presses, and it counts. The Drive mirror stays automatic on Free.

q: Over the storage cap, a person can move uploads into their Drive mirror. Then only Drive holds them.
r: Allow it, warned first: the moved file becomes a link we no longer guarantee. Checked before the move, logged, and offered only with Drive connected.

q: When a document is deleted for good, do we also delete the person's copy in GitHub or Drive?
r: Never. Our copy goes; theirs stays theirs, and the confirmation says so.

q: When someone deletes their account, what happens to their GitHub or Drive mirror?
r: Left in place, and our access to it is revoked. The files are theirs.

q: How long do we keep logs after an account is deleted?
r: Security log kept 365 days (the law asks for it). Keeping ordinary processing logs a year after deletion changes a promise to users, so your call; recommended no.

q: Should there be a third way to sign in, an email magic link?
r: Off at launch. If turned on later, a third button, never a form. Useful only when Google or GitHub sign-in is down.

q: Do we show the minimum age on the sign-in page?
r: One line under the buttons, no date of birth asked.

q: When a Pro payment fails, when do we remind, and when does Pro pause?
r: Remind on days 0, 3, 7 and 14, then pause Pro. Nothing is ever deleted. Separate from the trial, which you already decided.

q: If frontmatter ever shuts down, how much notice do people get?
r: 90 days, with export working throughout. 30 is too short.

q: What does Max cost? There is no price yet.
r: Metered per agent request, with the rate set in the admin panel from measured cost when the agents batch starts. No flat price now.

q: The tagline test: the pilot is too small to rank three lines properly. What do we do?
r: Use it as a screen, not a ranking: drop any line that 2 or fewer of 7 people get right. Ranking properly needs 15 to 39 people a line.

q: What does "the same theme as desktop" mean on the phone?
r: Three changes: the same surface layers, the same heading sizes, the same density. No separate phone colours. v8 already draws this; say if it looks right.

q: Where does the full "frontmatter" wordmark appear, and where only the fm mark?
r: Mark alone inside the app. Full wordmark on the sign-in page and on published pages only.

q: The plan puts the wordmark on the sign-in card; the drawn screen shows the mark.
r: Follow item 34: the sign-in page gets the full wordmark. Approving 34 settles this.

q: The five collapsible panels on the right: what is "Commands"?
r: The four drawn (Tags and bookmarks, Backlinks, History, Comments) plus Outline. "Commands" read as the Command K palette that already exists. Say if you meant something else.

q: Inviting someone gives both sides 5 AI credits. How do we stop people farming it?
r: Keep 5 each, and add a monthly cap per inviter, both set in the admin panel.

q: Are published pages findable on Google by default?
r: Conflicts with item 43. This item recommends yes, and saying "findable" when publishing. Item 43 recommends no. Pick one; your answer here sets both.

q: Is the Google-indexing setting one global switch, or per page?
r: Both: a global default plus a per-page choice when publishing. The default follows your answer to 38 (this item leans off).

q: Who buys the Windows code-signing certificate, and which one?
r: Get two written quotes in batch 1. Found so far: Sectigo from $536.25 a year, Certum from EUR 139. Windows shows "coming" until signed. Now urgent, since desktop ships early.

q: Do we offer an annual Pro plan?
r: Offer it as a choice. Note: at full use, annual loses about Rs 19 a month per user against monthly (a simulated figure).

q: Portfolio handles: what is a valid one, and who settles a dispute over a name?
r: Handles follow the same rules as page links. Disputes go through the grievance process; you decide outcomes.

q: Out of blueprint credits: can someone still run the questions?
r: Yes, on the standard question set. The generated files wait for the monthly reset or a top-up.

q: If "bring your own AI key" is switched off in the admin panel, what happens to keys people saved?
r: Stop using them, keep them stored, tell people, and restore on re-enable. Their calls move onto our cost meanwhile.

q: Mistral's free tier trains on what you send by default. Keep it in the free model chain?
r: Remove Mistral. Our sign-in promise is that we never train on documents.

q: Cloudflare R2 has no India region. Where does the government-required security log live?
r: In Firestore Mumbai (asia-south1), not R2. The plan's "R2 in Mumbai" line was wrong and gets corrected.

q: Which complaint deadline applies to us: the IT Rules, the consumer rules, or both?
r: Ask a lawyer. Until then we follow the stricter one.

q: The 2026 IT Rules cut the deadlines (7 days to resolve, 36 hours to remove, 3 hours on an order). Are we even an intermediary for published pages?
r: The deadlines are updated in the pack. Whether we are an intermediary needs a lawyer.

q: Which GST heading does a subscription editor fall under?
r: Ask a chartered accountant. Items 18, 19 and 20 are the same question in other files.

q: The tax heading (repeat of 17, in the pricing limits).
r: Settled with item 17.

q: The tax heading and the 2026 rate notification (repeat of 17).
r: Rate notification closed; heading settled with item 17.

q: The tax heading (repeat of 17, in the legal limits).
r: Settled with item 17.

q: The table of how often we sync to GitHub and Drive.
r: Adopted as the storage research proposed. Settled by item 2.

q: We said Indian cards get only one payment attempt. Is that true of Razorpay?
r: It was wrong. Razorpay retries subscriptions automatically. The record is corrected; we simply do not build our own retry scheduler.

q: 11 extra days added to batch 3 (editor and Doc mode) for the 18 September changes.
r: A proposed estimate; nothing to check until it is built.

q: 7 extra days added to batch 4 (sharing and the change queue).
r: A proposed estimate.

q: 10 to 12.5 extra days for the idea mode redesign.
r: A proposed estimate.

q: 2 extra days for the phone theme.
r: A proposed estimate.

q: 2 extra days for agents waiting on a change.
r: A proposed estimate.

q: Two different totals for the 18 September additions were both ours.
r: Use the itemised rows as the estimate; the headline figure came from an earlier draft of the same file.

q: Two keys that look the same but are written with different Unicode bytes: are they the same key?
r: Only if the bytes match. A near-match is refused and named, never guessed. This is the product's core rule.
